title: Chairs in a Row
statement: A row contains $13$ chairs. How many unordered pairs of different chairs from this row have an odd number of chairs strictly between them?
hints: Number the chairs $1$ to $13$ from left to right. If the chosen chairs are numbered $i$ and $j$ with $i<j$, how many chairs lie strictly between them?
Use parity. With the chairs numbered as above, there are $j-i-1$ chairs between chairs $i$ and $j$. Work out what this number being odd says about whether $i$ and $j$ are odd or even.

The number $j-i-1$ is odd exactly when $j-i$ is even, which happens exactly when $i$ and $j$ are both odd or both even. There are $7$ odd-numbered chairs and $6$ even-numbered chairs, so count the pairs within each group separately and add the two counts.
